reconstruction.scope: Specific standing Ritan ritual core: mapped low square gray altar/pale coping and corner strips, four straight cardinal stair flights with splayed pale cheeks, circular low red enclosure/green tiled coping, three open west stone portals and one closed red-leaf stone portal on each other cardinal approach. Original simplified pointed finials/scroll ends and shallow stone decoration. No roofed central temple, invented altar balustrade or copied inscriptions/sculpture/mural atlas. Other park pavilions, northwest auxiliary halls, Sun Worship mural and landscaping remain separate host context, not claimed authored in this ritual-core model.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Two ordinary pictured-state references: altar top about1.2m above its sampled upper ground envelope, nine nearby stair rises/four cardinal approaches. Enclosure red body1.55m above sampled grade plus green coping0.24m; west center stone portal4.7m, side portals4.3m, other three4.0m above their local threshold. Three west openings3.4m wide/2.65m tall; other gates3.2m wide with closed red leaves. Counts, leaf studs/scroll relief, heights and absolute threshold levels are estimates. The central altar has no roof/balustrade; old intact ceremonial interiors are not reconstructed.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Original standard6m Mapzen grid, native pedestrian courtyard/paths/water and all independent buildings remain unchanged. Only corresponding central platform shell35185801754351 is replaced. Altar occupied footing is buried below sampled ground and each narrow cardinal approach descends to sampled grade. Circular wall footings and coping follow the retained ground; gate footings are individually buried. No broad court/park slab, ground or water cutout, terrain flattening or invented whole-park reconstruction. Native coarse park ground cannot resolve archaeological paving and actual altar/stair thresholds; courtyard paving stays a host surface.
